{
  "candidate_rtl": "module decoder_8bit\n #(\n    parameter N = 8\n) (\n    input [N-1:0] in,\n    output reg [(1<<N)-1:0] out\n);\n    wire [15:0] low_dec;\n    wire [15:0] high_dec;\n    wire [255:0] decoded;\n\n    assign low_dec = 16'b1 << in[3:0];\n    assign high_dec = 16'b1 << in[7:4];\n\n    genvar k;\n    generate\n        for (k = 0; k < 256; k = k + 1) begin : gen_decode\n            assign decoded[k] = low_dec[k % 16] & high_dec[k / 16];\n        end\n    endgenerate\n\n    always @(*) begin\n        out = decoded;\n    end\nendmodule",
  "bottleneck": "The critical path is the 4-to-16 predecode for either input nibble followed by one final AND gate. The factored low/high decomposition limits decoder fanout and avoids an 8-level unfactored selection structure.",
  "rewrite": "Factor the 8-to-256 decode into two independent 4-to-16 one-hot decoders and combine one low-nibble term with one high-nibble term for each output bit. The generate loop preserves the original numerical bit ordering exactly.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "Expected improvement in maximum data arrival from reduced decode depth and lower intermediate fanout, subject to mapped-cell optimization and buffering.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "Uses two 16-bit predecode networks and 256 two-input combining gates. Factoring should be area-competitive with the original shift implementation while providing a more timing-friendly structure; no sequential, storage, or latency cost is introduced.",
  "functional_boundaries": "For every 8-bit binary input, exactly one output bit is 1 at index equal to in and all other output bits are 0. The module name, parameter declaration and default, port widths, output reg type, bit ordering, truncation width, and combinational behavior are preserved for N=8."
